targets.authors: Croninger, R. G., Rice, J. K., Rathbun, A., & Nishio, M.
targets.title: Teacher qualifications and early learning: Effects of certification, degree, and experience on first-grade student achievement.
targets.evidence_quote: To do so, we will replicate the Croninger et al. (2007) study using data since these reforms and compare the coefficients.
targets.outcome_quote: In the Croninger et al. (2007) study, the authors found that important teacher-level characteristics for achievement include having an elementary education degree. Teacher characteristics aggregated to the school level, such as the average number of courses teachers have taken in reading or having a high number of teachers with advanced degrees, are related to reading and mathematics achievement. Similar to the Croninger et al. (2007) study, the aggregate average of teachers who have had a reading course did positively relate to reading achievement, but no other teacher characteristics were statistically significant.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The discussion explicitly identifies one agreeing teacher-coursework association and other original teacher-characteristic associations absent in the new cohort.

reasoning: A different nationally representative ECLS-K cohort re-tests the published teacher-qualification findings. Other cited studies are contextual rather than targets.
